 Bournemouth 
 Bournemouth boss Marco Rose, speaking to Uefa : "I feel really good. I'm proud of the club, happy for the fans and proud of the lads. It was a great evening, a great result and a brilliant performance in every aspect. We were really sharp in everything, played our game and, it's a deserved win.
 "The way we got into the game, the effort, the attitude, the way we won balls and put pressure on Milan was great. We created chances, scored an early goal and kept the pressure high. This was Bournemouth, and this is what we wanted to show."

 FT: Bournemouth 3-0 AC Milan 
 AC Milan boss Ruben Amorim, speaking to Uefa: "It was not a great performance, because the game was over after 20 minutes. 
 "We defended quite well with 10 men and tried to push the game forward and take a risk near the end, but then the free-kick completely killed the game.
 "Now we must recover and think about the next one. We have to take lessons from this, and we cannot put ourselves in that position [after the red card] again. Now we must focus on the league and then try to win the next Europa match [vs Ferencváros] like we do in every game."

 'The thing I love about our team is the intensity we have' published at 22:29 BST 22 October 22:29 BST 22 October 
 FT: Bournemouth 3-0 AC Milan 
 Bournemouth 
 Bournemouth winger Justin Kluivert speaking to TNT Sport: "It means a lot. we come from two victories which gave us a good feeling going into this game. We just trusted in ourselves, it doesn't matter who we play against we just trust in ourselves. We know what we are capable of and I think we showed that tonight."
 On playing AC Milan: "AC Milan have a lot of history, it's a big club, and it's beautiful because what I didn't know before is that we have comparisons, the colours we have red and black, comes from AC Milan."
 On things finally clicking: "We know this run we have now, three wins, no goals conceded is something that I'm proud of, and we need to continue. We know how to continue we have done it before. We have a full squad now nearly fit, we have other guys coming back, so that competition makes it better. The thing I love about our team is the intensity we have, it doesn't matter who's in the starting 11, our intensity shows who we are and what we stand for, let's go full gas."
 On scoring the first penalty but not taking the second: "I think scored three one time in a game, but you got to be generous. I got to give my team-mates also the good feeling, and they also deserve to score penalty, because I also know they can score. We are a team, and not individuals."

 Bournemouth midfielder Ryan Christie speaking to TNT Sports: "What a night. The boys spoke about it before the game, listen it's a special night for the club but it becomes a lot more special if you go and win the game. Amazing, it's been such an experience playing in Europe, the fans have been amazing, the whole infrastructure the club have brought, in terms of the whole atmosphere coming into tonight and last week as well. It's incredible. It's a run of good results now, we need to keep going."
 On what it means to the fans: "It's mega. In terms of the story of the club it's ridiculous. Someone told me today, 15 years ago today we were 17th in League One I think so it's pretty incredible. So many of these fans have been here for this journey so to have nights like this and win as well is special."
 On momentum: "Now that we've got that bit of momentum. I think it's crucial when you've got so many games one after the other you just try and roll into the next one and keep the positivity. With the amount of games we've got, the gaffer has to use everyone in the squad and to be fair everyone has shown they can be called upon, the boys that came in tonight. Incredible tonight to come in and perform like that against a top team. Positivity going into the weekend.

 By Keifer MacDonald BBC Sport journalist A wasteful Sunderland missed the chance to make it three wins from three in the Europa League as they were held to a draw by Lech Poznan. 
 After victories over AZ Alkmaar and Portuguese second-tier side Torreense in their opening two games, the Black Cats were reminded of the challenges of European football as they surrendered their lead in the final 20 minutes against the Polish champions.
 Having slipped to the foot of the Premier League last weekend after suffering a fourth consecutive defeat, Sunderland initially showed little sign of feeling the pressure and took just two minutes to open the scoring in Poland.
 Winger Nilson Angulo capitalised on a loose pass from goalkeeper Mateusz Lis before crossing for Timur Tutierov to head home his first goal for the club, with the striker deputising for the injured Wilson Isidor and Brian Brobbey.
 Lech Poznan had a couple of chances to equalise during a chaotic opening period, but an impressive save from Robin Roefs kept Sunderland in front before the hosts' Daniel Hakans fired wide after being sent through on goal by Pablo Rodriguez.
 Sunderland manager Regis le Bris was left wondering how his side had not extended their advantage before the break, with the visitors registering eight shots on target and Malick Fofana striking the woodwork.
 The hosts should have punished Sunderland for their failure to convert earlier chances when the ball fell to an unmarked Leo Bengtsson at the back post shortly after the hour mark, but the substitute could not keep his volley on target.
 But there was time for Bengtsson to make amends with 20 minutes remaining, finding space inside the area after some sloppy Sunderland defending to score Lech Poznan's first Europa League goal of the campaign with a sweetly struck half-volley.
 After weathering a brief spell of pressure, Sunderland looked to have snatched a late winner for the second European away game in a row, but Chris Rigg's curling effort from outside the area whistled just past the post.
 Next up for Sunderland in the Europa League is a home match against Dinamo Zagreb on November 5 (20:00 GMT), while Lech Poznan will travel to Benfica at the same time.
 What did you think of Sunderland's performance?
 https://www.bbc.co.uk/send/u192436827 
 Positives for Le Bris despite Sunderland's wastefulness 
 There is rarely a bad away point in European football, but Sunderland will feel they should be returning to the Stadium of Light with all three points.
 After a dominant first-half display, the Black Cats looked a different side from the one that has struggled for both form and confidence in the Premier League this season.
 Angulo and Fofana provided flashes of attacking brilliance from either flank, and at times Sunderland threatened to overwhelm their opponents. But their failure to turn that dominance into goals ultimately cost them their perfect start in Europe.
 There were, of course, mitigating circumstances. Manager Le Bris was without first-choice strikers Brobbey and Isidor, as well as experienced defenders Thomas Meunier and Dan Ballard, leaving him short of options as his side's energy faded in the second half.
 The draw does little to derail Sunderland's hopes of reaching the Europa League knockout stages, but the bigger test await in the Premier League.
 Le Bris will hope the quality and intensity his side showed in spells in Poland carry over into domestic action, starting against Leeds United on Sunday.
